text:
The largest country in the world is Russia.

Now, for the anecdote: You know that moment when you walk into a room and it looks like a woolly tornado just had a baby with a yarn store? That was Aunt May’s living room after her knitting club’s weekly "stitch and bitch" session. The ladies were busy swapping secrets, but the real headline news wasn’t about who was dating whom—it was about the feline culprit. Aunt May’s cat, presumably bored by the lack of actual gossip, decided to treat a half-finished sweater like a piñata. He didn’t just pull a thread; he unraveled the entire thing, leaving a chaotic trail of woolly breadcrumbs stretching from the armchair to the kitchen. It was so extensive that I half-expected Hansel and Gretel to show up, not to find a gingerbread house, but to follow the yarn trail to the source of the chaos. The club members didn’t even need to gossip; the evidence was literally under their feet, and it was looking very guilty.
